Dogs diagnosed with glioma, an aggressive brain tumor, often experience limited benefit from standard treatments such as radiation therapy alone. This clinical trial is evaluating a novel investigational drug called bisaminoquinoline-13 (BAQ-13) that may help improve how brain tumors respond to radiation therapy.


BAQ-13 works by blocking a process called autophagy, which cancer cells use to survive treatment. This study will evaluate whether BAQ-13 can safely reach brain tumors, be tolerated by dogs receiving radiation therapy, and show early signs of effectiveness.

Please note that we have many inquiries coming through for this study, with limited spaces left. We ask that you be patient as we sort through inquires and do our best to get back to each individual.

Please note we are only enrolling cats diagnosed with the DRY form of FIP at this time

Pets and their owners must reside within close proximity of Davis, CA. Before we can enroll your cat, we require a full set of veterinary records to be sent to our office by your veterinarian.

Feline infectious peritonitis (FIP) is a fatal disease of cats with no available FDA-approved treatment or vaccine. Antiviral drugs that decrease virus replication have been investigated in cats with FIP with promising results. In this trial, your cat will receive an investigational oral antiviral drug.

If you are looking for more information on current FIP treatments and news, please visit this site: https://ccah.vetmed.ucdavis.edu/cats/resources/general-feline-infectious-peritonitis-resources.
